claims.text: Fear of missing out (FOMO) mediates the link between psychopathological symptoms and negative consequences of using social networking sites via mobile devices.
Social networking intensity mediates the link between psychopathological symptoms and negative consequences of using social networking sites via mobile devices.
FOMO and social networking intensity mediate the link between psychopathology and negative consequences of mobile social networking site use through different mechanisms.
For adolescent girls, feeling depressed triggers higher social networking site involvement.
For adolescent boys, anxiety triggers higher social networking site involvement.

evidence.description: Structural equation modeling of online survey data from 1,468 Spanish-speaking Latin-American social media users aged 16-18 showed that FOMO mediates the link between psychopathology and negative consequences of mobile SNS use (CERM).

Structural equation modeling of online survey data from 1,468 Spanish-speaking Latin-American social media users aged 16-18 showed that Social Networking Intensity (SNI) mediates the link between psychopathology and negative consequences of mobile SNS use (CERM).
Structural equation modeling revealed that FOMO and SNI mediate the psychopathology-CERM relationship through distinct mechanisms.
Structural equation modeling showed a specific link where feeling depressed triggers higher SNS involvement among girls.
Structural equation modeling showed a specific link where anxiety triggers higher SNS involvement among boys.

methodologies.name: Structural Equation Modeling on Online Survey Data
methodologies.description: Analysis using structural equation modeling on data collected via HADS, SNI, FOMOs, and CERM questionnaires.
datasets: Online survey of 1468 Spanish-speaking Latin-American social media users aged 16 to 18
conditions: Questionnaire on negative consequences of using SNS via mobile device (CERM)
